title: The First Text Message Ever Sold for Over 100,000 Euros

scenes.text: A 15-character text message sold for over 100,000 euros.
scenes.keywords: old mobile phone text message screen

scenes.text: Neil Papworth, a Vodafone programmer, sent it in December 1992 to his colleague Richard Jarvis.
Nearly thirty years later it went up for auction in Paris.
The buyer got a digital copy of the message, an NFT, and the money went to the UN refugee agency.
Two words. Fifteen characters. Over a hundred thousand euros.

description:
A 15-character text sold for over 100,000 euros.
The world's first SMS read Merry Christmas and was sent in December 1992 by Vodafone programmer Neil Papworth. In 2021 it sold as an NFT at an auction in Paris, with proceeds going to the UN refugee agency.
What was the last text you sent? Comment below.
first_comment: The first text said Merry Christmas. What do you think the first words of the next big invention should be?
